type.evidence: README Inputs: "FASTQ file or BAM-file from singe-end or paird-end sequencing platforms"; from_bam sub-command takes "--bam" plus an STR config bed. README examples use ucsc.hg19.fasta, so the reference build differs from hg38.

fixture_path.evidence: File tree contains example/test_data/test.bam; README example: "--bam example/test_results/alignments/test.bam".

caveats: --ref_bed expects an 11-column STR configuration file (chr/start/end/period/.../flanking sequences), not a plain BED; /data/in/regions.bed must be in that format. example/ref_test.bed is the in-repo template.
Example coordinates/reference are hg19 (ucsc.hg19.fasta, ref_test.bed); a hg38-aligned BAM needs an hg38 STR config file or results will be wrong.

usearch is required but is licensed; the Dockerfile fetches it from a personal license URL ("drive5.com/cgi-bin/upload3.py?license=...") which will likely fail. Supply the usearch binary at /usr/bin/usearch during image build.
The from_fastq mode needs a bwa-indexed reference (.amb/.ann/.bwt/.pac/.sa); only hg38.fa + .fai are mounted, so index at build time or use from_bam.
Dockerfile assumes code lives in a ./STRsearch subdirectory (COPY ./STRsearch /STRsearch), but conf.py, pipeline.py and scripts/ are at the repository root; adjust paths for the /opt/tool checkout.
Dockerfile pins ubuntu:16.04, Miniconda 4.3.31 and old bioconda builds (samtools 1.7, bedtools 2.17.0); these pins may not resolve on a modern Ubuntu 22.04 base and may need updating.
--sex is a required argument for from_bam; the example uses male, which affects Y-locus handling.
